source_gloss.salka_ereyga: lexical stem/root carrying the core meaning
source_gloss.salkordhiye: derivational extension that can add meaning and alter participant structure
source_gloss.isrogrog: inflection expressing tense and also aspect/mood in the source description

rule: The lexical stem represents the core lexical meaning; examples include cun, qor, xir, and dil.
A verbal stem may itself contain a noun base plus a derivational suffix.
A salkordhiye can add meaning to the stem and can change the number/roles of participants licensed by the verb.
The source analyzes -is here as a derivational extension that changes an intransitive Class-I stem into a transitive Class-II verb.
The person element expresses agreement between the verb and the sentence subject/agent in the source's analysis.
The isrogrog component expresses tense, aspect, and mood; elsewhere in the same discussion the source also treats negative paradigms separately.
The source states that the combination of person-agreement material and tense inflection yields five distinct surface patterns used across eight pronoun/person categories in the illustrated paradigm.
implementation_note: The analyzer must permit one surface verb form to map to multiple person/gender analyses and resolve them using subject/clitic/context evidence rather than suffix matching alone.

rule: Do not infer semantic roles from word order or verb suffixes alone. Derivational morphology can change valency, and person morphology can be syncretic across multiple pronoun categories; semantic-role analysis must combine lemma/derivation, subject evidence, object/clitic evidence, and sentence context.
